neighbours.label: tokens in prose about earning, selling or paying for work and goods (economic exchange of value); the same sentence frames about non-economic matters stay quiet
fire: Freelancers set their rates by the value they deliver to each client.
Most farmers earn their income from selling crops at the local market.
A good salesperson knows how to price a product for what buyers will pay.
Workers trade their time and skills for wages paid by employers.
Companies make a profit when revenue from sales exceeds their costs.
If you do work you enjoy, the money tends to follow over time.
Shoppers exchange cash for goods that they value more than the price.
Consultants are paid to solve problems that clients cannot solve alone.
quiet: Hikers set their pace by the weather they meet on each trail.
Most farmers spend their mornings walking along the edge of the forest.
A good storyteller knows how to pause before the ending of a tale.
Children trade their stickers and cards during the school break.
Rivers flood the valley when rain from the hills exceeds the banks.
If you walk every day, the stiffness tends to fade over time.
Neighbours exchange greetings over the fence on summer evenings.
Gardeners are happy to watch plants grow that they planted themselves.
